summary: Workcell's skills are strong on orchestration process (dispatch contracts, deterministic merge/render scripts, human gates, evals) but carry almost no code-design method: the only architecture vocabulary in the repo is two sentences in code-refactor, code-review has no architecture lens, and reviewer agents get four vague style flags. mattpocock/skills supplies exactly the missing layer — codebase-design is a portable, closed-glossary design method (depth-as-leverage, the deletion test, seam/adapter rules, testability rules, a 4-tier dependency classification) and improve-codebase-architecture is a report-first architecture-audit workflow whose shape (git-history scoping, sub-agent exploration, HTML candidate report for human triage, ADR-conflict policy) maps almost one-to-one onto patterns Workcell already has. Port the content — the glossary, principles, and workflow steps — into Workcell's existing skill shapes (references/ files, lenses, research/refactor survey steps) rather than importing the single-agent skills wholesale.

recommendations.title: Port the codebase-design glossary and principles as a shared design-heuristics reference
recommendations.detail: Create a design-heuristics reference (e.g. skills/code-refactor/references/design-heuristics.md, cross-linked from code-review and plan) carrying the closed glossary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality — with banned synonyms), the four principles (depth is a property of the interface; the deletion test; the interface is the test surface; one adapter = hypothetical seam, two = real), the three testability rules, and DEEPENING.md's 4-tier dependency classification. This fills the repo's only real content gap: no skill or doc currently teaches a design method, and code-refactor/code-analysis are SKILL.md-only with no references/ today.

recommendations.title: Upgrade code-refactor's survey step with the ported heuristics
recommendations.detail: code-refactor's survey currently lists six smells in one sentence. Give its researcher agents the deletion test, depth-as-leverage, the adapter-count seam rule, and git-log hot-spot scoping (YAGNI: scan where the history shows churn, not the whole tree) from improve-codebase-architecture's exploration step, plus the 'replace, don't layer' test policy (delete implementation-level tests once interface-level tests exist) when a module is deepened.

recommendations.title: Adopt improve-codebase-architecture's report-first triage as the front half of code-refactor (or a research preset)
recommendations.detail: Before any refactor work, produce a candidate report for human triage: one card per deepening opportunity with Files/Problem/Solution/Benefits, a recommendation-strength badge (Strong / Worth exploring / Speculative), an explicit ADR-conflict callout policy (only surface a conflict when friction justifies reopening the ADR; offer to record an ADR when the human rejects a candidate), and a hard rule of not designing interfaces before the human picks. Render it with Workcell's existing Foundry Zero report tooling rather than the upstream Tailwind/Mermaid scaffold.

recommendations.title: Add Design-It-Twice to plan/new-feature for interface decisions
recommendations.detail: The DESIGN-IT-TWICE process — spawn 3+ parallel agents, each forced to design the interface a radically different way (minimal surface, max flexibility, optimise for the common caller, ports & adapters), compare on depth/locality/seam placement, end with one opinionated recommendation — is a natural fit for Workcell's existing fan-out orchestration and would slot into plan or new-feature at the point an interface is being chosen.

recommendations.title: Close the architecture-lens gap in code-review deliberately
recommendations.detail: code-review's lens set (correctness, tests, security, performance, api-contract, backend, integrations, frontend) has no architecture lens; design judgment today is four style flags bolted onto the correctness lens, while code-analysis explicitly routes design to code-refactor. Either add an architecture lens reference (analogous to references/frontend-review.md) built on the ported glossary, or state in the reviewer bodies that module-design findings belong to code-refactor — the current in-between leaves reviewers with no method.

recommendations.title: Borrow small authoring conventions where Workcell lacks them
recommendations.detail: Worth copying: `disable-model-invocation: true` frontmatter on human-gated command skills; the project-memory convention of a domain-vocabulary file that skills read so seam names match domain language (Workcell's wiki/AGENTS.md could carry this); and the glossary-enforced, no-hedging report tone. Not worth copying: the upstream repo has no eval harness for its skills (Workcell's evals/cases is ahead) and its single-agent skill shape conflicts with ADR 0007's pure-orchestrator contract — port content, not process shape.
